title: UDLM Composite Service Catalog Item
$comment: The canonical name for this tier is Template (naming-charter, Canonical glossary). 'Composite Service' names the same thing: composite describes the structure, while this tier IS a definition authored once and ordered many times, and only Template carries that. Composite Service was considered and rejected as a second name for one function — two names cost every reader the mapping. Alignment: croadfeldt/udlm#405.
description: The catalog-level Composite Service definition (docs/spec/foundations/template-composition-model.md): constituent resource types, their dependency edges, their declared data-movement bindings, and their failure classification — everything the control plane needs to expand a catalog request into a Composite Entity. This is item (2) of the [D8] machine-validatable-surface program (data-model-core §2) and the schema evidence for the application model: an 'application' IS a Composite catalog item. Cross-file constraints (depends_on/bindings.from_component must reference sibling component_ids; the depends_on graph must be acyclic; a binding's from_component must appear in that constituent's depends_on) are not expressible in pure JSON Schema — registry/tools/validate.py enforces them as semantic checks.

record_type.description: Top-level dispatch discriminator. Instance-record kinds are distinguished by record_type going forward; resource_type (realized entities) and group_class (DCMGroups) remain the legacy discriminators for the pre-existing record kinds. registry/tools/validate.py dispatches on record_type first.

uuid.description: Stable RFC 9562 v4 identity of this catalog item, minted once at creation (identifier-scheme §2.1; version nibble + variant bits pattern-enforced). Composite Entities produced from this item reference it — never the reverse.

handle.description: ADVISORY human-readable identity (docs/spec/contracts/identifier-scheme.md §3), e.g. org/catalog/three-tier-web-app. The uuid is the authoritative identity; never resolve by handle alone.

name.description: Human-readable name of the Composite Service, e.g. ApplicationStack.WebApp.

version.description: Major.Minor.Revision of this catalog item (registry/VERSIONING.md semantics). Consumers pin catalog_ref to a version.

status.description: Catalog lifecycle status: active | deprecated | retired, with the universal deprecation fields when deprecated (the universal deprecation model, docs/spec/foundations/layering-and-versioning.md).

deprecation_date.description: RFC 3339 instant, normalized to UTC ('Z'), seconds precision minimum (common-elements.md §Timestamps).

sunset_date.description: RFC 3339 instant, normalized to UTC ('Z'), seconds precision minimum (common-elements.md §Timestamps).

replacement_uuid.description: The successor catalog item, if deprecated.

tenant_uuid.description: REQUIRED owning Tenant — the uuid of an `Grouping` of group class `tenant_boundary` (registry/classes/access/grouping/_base.yaml), consistent with [D3] (data-model-core §5): every record belongs to exactly one Tenant. Ownership only — consumption of this catalog item by other tenants happens via requests and cross-tenant authorization grants, never by shared ownership.

consumer_fields.description: The consumer-facing parameter surface: what a consumer supplies in the Intent record (template-composition-model.md §3.1) alongside the catalog_ref. Expansion maps these into constituent specs via layer assembly.

default.description: Default value when the consumer omits the field (any JSON type, matching `type`).

enum_values.description: Allowed values — required when type = enum.

metadata.description: Human-facing context, same shape as realized-entity: operational commentary lives in notes — data ABOUT the record, never used for resolution.

notes.description: Auditable operational notes: each entry is attributed and timestamped — never an anonymous mutable blob.

at.description: When recorded. RFC 3339 instant, normalized to UTC ('Z'), seconds precision minimum (common-elements.md §Timestamps).

author.description: Who/what recorded it (person, agent+session, or process uuid).
